records.primary_i_can: I can explain why an object moving at constant speed in a straight line can be in equilibrium and use the equilibrium rule to reason about upward/downward and left/right forces.
records.i_can: I can explain why an object moving at constant speed in a straight line can be in equilibrium and use the equilibrium rule to reason about upward/downward and left/right forces.
records.evidence_job: Explain that constant straight-line velocity can occur in equilibrium and use the equilibrium rule to reason about unknown upward/downward or left/right force components.
records.student_action: Explain that constant straight-line velocity can occur in equilibrium and use the equilibrium rule to reason about unknown upward/downward or left/right force components.
records.student_text: A stage platform moves in a straight line at constant speed. Horizontally, a motor pulls with 72 N to the right while resistance acts to the left. Using \(\Sigma F_x=0\), determine the resistance force.
records.student_html:
A stage platform moves in a straight line at constant speed. Horizontally, a motor pulls with 72 N to the right while resistance acts to the left. Using \(\Sigma F_x=0\), determine the resistance force.

  1. 72 N to the left
  2. 99 N
  3. 45 N
  4. cannot be determined because the object is moving

choices.text: cannot be determined because the object is moving

records.solution_text: Constant straight-line velocity means equilibrium, so 72 N right must be balanced by 72 N left.
records.solution_html: Constant straight-line velocity means equilibrium, so 72 N right must be balanced by 72 N left.
source_basis: accepted Bank Map record U1-S4-WU1-Q3: Explain that constant straight-line velocity can occur in equilibrium and use the equilibrium rule to reason about unknown upward/downward or left/right force components.

records.student_text: Which row gives a falsifiable claim with a workable measurement route?
records.student_html:
Which row gives a falsifiable claim with a workable measurement route?

OptionClaimPossible evidence
AIncreasing the number of rubber bands changes launch distance.Count rubber bands and measure launch distance.
BThe universe likes smooth tracks.“Likes” is not measurable.
CRed carts have stronger personalities.Personality is not a physical measurement.
DThe cart moves better when it is happy.No measurable condition is defined.
  1. Claim A
  2. Claim B
  3. Claim C
  4. Claim D
records.solution_text: A claim is testable when observations or measurements could provide evidence for or against it.

  1. The opposing forces can balance so their vector sum is zero even though individual forces are present.
  2. An object at rest cannot have any forces acting.
  3. Inertia creates an upward force that removes all other forces.
  4. Only gravitational force matters when speed is zero.
